The ephemeral path is unguarded because SendEphemeralPost never calls Post.IsValid.

claim: The new hardcoded byte-based check `maxLength := 65535; if len(o.Text) > maxLength` contradicts the configurable rune-based limit actually enforced downstream (Post.IsValid checks utf8.RuneCountInString against the DB-derived maxPostSize, default 16383 runes). It is both too loose (16384-65535 bytes passes but is rejected downstream) and, on a deployment with a manually enlarged posts.message column, too strict — an ASCII response over 65535 bytes that previously succeeded end-to-end is now hard-rejected at parse time.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: Hardcoded byte-based `65535` cap contradicts the configurable, rune-based limit enforced downstream
